# General polytope contact and the exact support-gap test

This is a support-geometric lemma for n=1. It does not supply a general cap-union volume estimate or a proof of OC.

Let C be convex with positive sampled fibers D=K_-1 and K=K_0. Suppose K is a full-dimensional polytope, D is contained in K, and D meets EVERY facet hyperplane of K. Write a facet representation

    K=intersection_r {x:n_r·x<=b_r}.

Then h_D(n_r)=h_K(n_r)=b_r. Concavity of the fiber support function in the real base coordinate gives h_{C_t}(n_r)<=b_r for every t>=0 in the projection. Hence EVERY real right-hand fiber lies in K. Point contact with each facet is sufficient for this inclusion; positive facet area is not needed.

Now suppose Y=(0,y) is an actual deepest source of the positive-width model and K1 is another deepest fiber. For a selected actual cap with margin

    a z+u·(x-y),  w=h Gamma(u)>0,

assume its smoothed integrand vanishes on D and its outside strip coarea vanishes on K1. Strict actual-source exclusion forces its integrand to vanish on all of K1 as well. The two complete misses imply

    -a+h_D(u)-u·y<=-w,
     a+h_K1(u)-u·y<=-w.

Therefore

    h_K1(u)<=2u·y-h_D(u)-2w=:b(u).                  (1)

For a finite bundle B of such caps, the exact geometric containment is

    K1 subset K_B:=K intersect intersection_(u in B){x:u·x<=b(u)}.

If just ONE selected cap satisfies

    b(u)<[h_K(u)+min_K u]/2,                         (2)

then no fiber at base2 can exist. Indeed concavity gives

    h_K2(u)<=2h_K1(u)-h_K(u)<min_K u,

whereas K2 subset K gives h_K2(u)>=min_K u if K2 is nonempty. The projection is an interval, so every larger integer is absent too. Thus K1 is globally exposed among sampled fibers, a fact special to this one-integer-variable setting.

If, in addition, a rigorous volume estimate gives |K_B|<2Gamma_d|K| by a fixed margin, then for sufficiently small positive width the exposed-fiber half-volume upper bound contradicts deepestness of K1. To track smoothing explicitly, choose a nonzero continuous functional ell, let C_ell bound the ell-marginal density of uniform measure on K, and let G_ell bound the actual covariance norm Gamma(ell). Opposite own smoothed caps have combined mass at most

    |K1|+2hG_ell C_ell.

One has mass at most |K_B|/2+hG_ell C_ell and can be isolated by a finite base tilt. The ordinary centroid of K supplies raw lower bound Gamma_d|K| in the whole mixed set. Thus the exact sufficient inequality is

    |K_B|/2+hG_ell C_ell<Gamma_d|K|.                 (3)

This is a directly checkable support-and-volume certificate. It neither assumes that contact alone makes |K_B| small nor identifies the cap weights with cap-union volume. In the d=4 thin-edge bundle, (2) is the bound .41<.5 and (3) follows from the three-coordinate inclusion-exclusion calculation. In the full-parity triangle-square counterexample, the corresponding complementary-cap bound is near1 while K's support midpoint is1/2; (2) fails, allowing the further right reservoir. This explains a precise geometric difference between those two actual constructions.

# General polytope contact and the exact support-gap test

**One-integer polytope contact and reflected support exclusion**

Let n=1 and let D=K_(-1) subset K=K_0 be positive fibers of an actual convex body, with K a full-dimensional polytope and D meeting every facet hyperplane of K. Then every real right-hand fiber lies in K. In the source's positive-width model suppose Y=(0,y) is deepest and K_1 is another deepest fiber. For a selected cap with margin a z+u.(x-y) and width w=h Gamma(u)>0, assume it misses D and its outside strip coarea on K_1 vanishes, so that the source-exclusion hypothesis also makes it miss all of K_1. The two miss inequalities for this same cap imply h_(K_1)(u)<=2u.y-h_D(u)-2w=:b(u). If b(u)<[h_K(u)+min_(x in K)u.x]/2 for even one such cap, no fiber at integer base 2 or later can exist. A volume contradiction requires the additional separately checked volume bound from the source.

Scope limits: Retains all contact and miss assumptions. The final volume comparison is conditional, not a consequence of contact alone. Higher-dimensional off-line fibers cannot be discarded.
